text:
oliver: Heads-up — post-deploy role-rename-compat we got a compliance flag from audit: several permission-change events for role renames are missing in the audit log for org-scoped updates. Auditor noticed gaps for May-June rollups.

zara: Which deploy/tag and which orgs? @jin can you triage?

oliver: Deploy: role-rename-compat-2026-08-15. Affected orgs: org-808, org-909. Example: we renamed `viewer`->`read-only` internally; DB shows new alias but audit stream doesn't have corresponding `rbac.role_change` events for the project-level backfills. Auditor counted mismatch between DB and audit-events.

jin: Repro: compare DB rows vs audit stream. DB: `select count(*) from rbac_roles where org_id='org-808' and role_alias='read-only';` -> 124 rows. Audit stream query `audit.events where resource='rbac_roles' and org_id='org-808' and event_type='rbac.role_change' and timestamp between '2026-05-01' and '2026-06-30'` -> 10 events only. That's a big discrepancy.

audit-bot: audit pipeline: migration-run id=mig-20260815-04 by svc rbac-migrator@infra at 2026-08-15T03:05Z. Note: audit-forwarder reported transient backpressure to the event bus during 03:06:00Z..03:09:40Z and dropped 47 events (buffer_full). Forwarder inserted tombstones but didn't retry.

kms-bot: KMS: no decrypt errors during that window for key=projects/ri/locations/global/keyRbac. KMS logs look healthy.

zara: So root cause sounds like audit-forwarder backpressure. Why would audit events be tied to role-rename writes? Migrator emits both DB updates and audit events; if forwarder failed the DB writes may have succeeded while events were dropped. That's a compliance issue: our audit trail must be durable or we must emit a replayable change log.

jin: Quick check: `select min(updated_at), max(updated_at) from rbac_roles where org_id='org-808' and role_alias='read-only';` -> 2026-08-15T03:05:12..03:09:01. Matches forwarder backpressure window.

sec-oncall: Impact: High for compliance (missing audit events). Customers with stringent audits could be impacted. Flag P1. Need incident and remediation: 1) capture list of DB changes missing audit events, 2) re-emit audit events for those changes, 3) harden forwarder and add at-least-once guarantees or persistent queueing.

oliver: For immediate mitigation I can run a diff script that selects recent rbac_role writes and replays audit events using the migrator's run_id, with annotation `replay=true`. Example repro command I used locally:

```
# find DB rows without audit events
WITH recent AS (
  SELECT id, org_id, resource_id, role_alias, updated_at
  FROM rbac_roles
  WHERE updated_at BETWEEN '2026-08-15T03:00:00Z' AND '2026-08-15T03:15:00Z'
)
SELECT r.id FROM recent r
LEFT JOIN audit.events a ON a.resource_id = r.id AND a.event_type = 'rbac.role_change'
WHERE a.id IS NULL;
```

zara: Good. Let's capture that list and then re-emit events via the audit replay API (audit-service supports replay with `replay=true` and preserves original timestamps). But we must record this replay in audit itself (meta-audit) so auditors know these were replayed.

audit-bot: Opening INC-20260815-21 and attaching forwarder logs + missing-event list placeholder.

jin: I started a replay job for org-808 with run id replay-20260815-1, sending batched events and recording an audit entry `audit.replay` per batch. I'm throttling at 50 events/s to not overload the bus.

infra-bot: replay job queued: audit-replay org=org-808 run_id=replay-20260815-1 (eta ~60s)

sec-oncall: Also requirement: add test failing if forwarder drops events silently. We should change forwarder to persist to a local disk-backed queue before acknowledging DB-side completion. Also add alert when forwarder buffer_full occurrences > 0 in 5m window.

oliver: Frontend/UI effect: none — this is audit-only. But we need to inform compliance team. I'll draft a short notification and include replay run ids.

zara: Replays underway. For org-909 I'll kick off replay-20260815-2 after verifying the missing list. Jin, please include a CSV of missing row ids in the incident ticket and link to the replay job logs.

jin: Replay logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/replay-20260815-1. Replayed 112 events for org-808, all acknowledged by audit-service. I also created audit entries `audit.replay` for transparency.

kms-bot: Confirmed: no KMS issues. Good to document that KMS wasn't the cause here.

sec-oncall: Follow-ups (postmortem): 1) make audit-forwarder durable (disk-backed queue or broker with ack), 2) make migrator emit an idempotent change-log table so replays can be derived even if forwarder fails, 3) alerting on forwarder buffer_full and bus backpressure, 4) run replay for all orgs touched by the deploy and notify compliance. Assign owners in INC-20260815-21.

zara: Noted. Also add a short runbook step: when forwarder reports dropped events, create `audit.replay` entry, generate missing-list using the CTE and run replay job.

oliver: Closing immediate P1 after replays complete for affected orgs. Will update auditor and attach INC ticket. Thanks all. :lock:
